However, as a series game of Ultimate Ninja Storm, have not played the previous game or do not understand the background of the game plot will lead to the lack of the game experience, and the music in this game is not so brilliant compared to other elements- of course, I am not talking the anime music and actors, is the music and sound effects in this game.

I'm going to be straight up honest with you, and say this game is pretty fun. I'm a Naruto fan, and a long time fighting game lover, so of course I'm going to love STORM 4, but instead of making this review telling you how much I love it, I'll attempt to be as unbias as possible and label the good and bad. 

First of all, you should know playing this will spoil the Naruto Anime/Manga if you haven't watched/read either one, as it very well tells you the story from the point Naruto breaks Tobi's mask, to the very end of the series. Does that mean you should play the other STORM's? Or go finish the Anime and Manga? Well, it's all a matter of preference, because really, the game did spoil a LOT, but that doesn't mean I didn't enjoy it! I think I enjoyed it more than actually watching the Anime.

Next, you should know STORM 4 now focuses more on slideshows. If you played or watched the previous STORM games, you'd know that it was all cinematic 3D cut scenes, while STORM 4 relies more on slideshows from the Anime. It was obviously a lazy move, and I very much prefer the animated cutscenes MUCH more. Not to say it doesn't have those cool 3D animated scenes, just not nearly as much as anybody would like. 

If you also haven't heard already, this is their last Naruto game, (Or just their last STORM game, not exactly sure) meaning there won't be anymore. Feel like picking up a Naruto game? This is the best choice hands down.

However, the game has a lot of negative aspects to it, which some do tend to annoy me.

The support characters from the previous STORM games are not included in here, which to me, is yet another lazy move. Online connections haven't changed much, they removed still haven't added back wall combat, and the game in gameplay wise isn't much different from past STORM games.

The game graphically, however, has a lot of nice animations and particles that make it look like a 3D anime, which I quite like.

Quick overview of fixes for common starting bugs, basically so people don't downvote the game because of these - 

- Audio Crackling, if this happens go to your audio playback settings and set it to 24 bits 48000HZ.

- Slow Motion, this was caused by setting the game to 60fps for me and the sure fix was setting it to 30 again. Not a problem everyone has with 60fps but try 30 if you have it just incase.

- Achievements and other info locking into black bars, this is simply cause by Steam Overlay. Just go to Library -> Right click game -> Properties -> Disable Steam Overlay.

- Game not loading in Fullscreen after setting it to On previously, just turn it off and back on again. Also if this does not work go to your config.ini file in Naruto file and change windowed to 0, even if it already says 0 delete and retype it.

[h1]There's no real need to give a comprehensive review for this game.[/h1]

(For one, don't spend $29 on this game, [b]it regularly goes on sale for $6[/b], just add it to your wishlist at the top.)

[h1]Overview[/h1]

This game is 6yrs old, runs on almost any PC(literally), is visually superior to most Anime games to date, looking exactly like the Anime and is [b]still relevant in 2022 & beyond.[/b] It's online player base has peaked 7k players this year & holds steady with 1k players daily, that's not factoring in PS4/XB1 players who will move to PC if they want to keep playing this game after Sony/Microsoft kill online connectivity for those consoles.

It is the best Arena Fighter & has effectively been the sole innovator of this genre, it is [b]simple/easy to play while still being rewarding & offers incredible complexity to the gameplay if you want to be competitive[/b] and master the mechanics. It rewards both casual players and enjoyers of skill/tech-based: 3v3 combat

The difference between this game and previous Storm games is the Counter System isn't broken(S:Revolution), ability to Switch Characters during gameplay is easily the best innovation, [b]combining those two = Tech.[/b]

[h1]Story[/h1]

Storm 4 actually completed the story before the Anime/Manga, while giving a faithful and honestly amazing representation of the journey wrapping the 4th Great Ninja War & the events after [spoiler]Obito Uchiha's relveal[/spoiler]. CC2 is clearly the best in the game when it comes to accurately & masterfully meeting/exceeding your expectations; [b]Setting a standard for what a Manga/Anime Video Game Adaptation should be[/b] when done with this level of budget.

It is the best Video Game Adaptation of an Anime, [b]it is alone worth it for the story alone..[/b] But the gameplay will likely keep you engaged for a while after you complete the story and unlock the characters.

[h1]TL;DR[/h1]

This game is honestly an 8.5/10, it's the best Video Game adaptation of an Anime, Storm 4 is visually a superior anime title that honestly immerses you into the game with the unparalleled Anime/Manga-like visuals alone, while also running on basically any modern computer. The combat  single handily is [b]worthy of being called the best Arena Fighter[/b] to exist and the franchise(STORM) has been the only innovator of this genre.

For $6 it's really not the worst thing you could buy, if you're a fan of Naruto then it's [b]the only Naruto game worth getting imo.[/b]

And [b]yes it runs on Steam Deck[/b](online, all controls, no anti-cheat), despite the "Unsupported" Verification rating.

[h1]New Players[/h1]

If you want to move beyond being a casual player or simply want an advantage over your friends there are [b]several guides/tutorials online that will teach you how to play[/b] characters, advance your technique, etc. I'll recommend a channel for you to overview if you so choose to learn more and become a better ninja.

Naruto Shippuden: Ultimate Ninja Storm 4 - Believe It, It's Awesome!
Hey there, fellow Naruto fan! Just finished rocking out in Naruto Shippuden: Ultimate Ninja Storm 4, and let me tell you, it was a blast! This game is like the ultimate Naruto experience – super fun and full of all the things we love about the series.

Story Mode Like Your Favorite Anime: Remember those epic Naruto fights from the show? Story mode feels like you're right in the middle of them! The boss battles are crazy intense, especially the final one (but I won't spoil anything!). Plus, those moments where you get to take control during big fights with Quick Time Events? They had my heart pounding!

Jutsu for Days!: This game is all about those awesome jutsu attacks, and they do not disappoint. Seeing Naruto unleash a Rasengan or Kakashi pull off his Chidori is amazing – just like in the anime! There are tons of characters to pick from too, so you can find your perfect fighter and spam their coolest moves.

Button Mashing with a Ninja Twist: The controls are easy to learn, so anyone can jump in and start throwing down. But there's also a surprising amount of depth here. Learning combos and mastering special techniques for each character is super rewarding. And let's not forget those epic Awakening moments – they're like watching the most awesome anime cutscene ever, right in the middle of the fight!

Looking Like a Ninja Masterpiece: The graphics in this game are fantastic. The characters look like they jumped right out of the Naruto universe, and the environments are detailed and exciting to explore. It feels like you're really there in the Hidden Leaf Village or running through the battlefield.

A Couple of Minor Dings: Alright, so it wasn't absolutely perfect. Some of the missions outside the story mode felt a bit repetitive, and playing online could be a bit glitchy at times.

Final Verdict: Believe It!: Even with a few small bumps, Naruto Shippuden: Ultimate Ninja Storm 4 is incredible for any Naruto fan. It's an action-packed adventure that captures the spirit of the series perfectly. If you're looking for a game that will make you feel like the ultimate ninja, look no further! Just remember, Dattebayo! Believe it!

You should definitly buy this game if you are a Naruto fan or a fighting genre player.

FOR STARTERS:
Storm 4 is undoubtedly the best Naruto game overall. It was initially released in 2016 and has since become the best-selling anime game on the market. However, reading this, you wouldn't believe that its development was plagued by budget issues and other problems. And the results? Yes, we can still see them in the final release. And those are exactly my main issues with this game.

•STORY MODE
Right off the bat, half of the story, which covers the anime's final arc, is told through slideshows with fancy after effects. (Really poor tbh) This is because CC2 (the developer) had to cut MANY of the cutscenes they intended to create in-engine due to time constraints and budget issues with Bandai Namco. So, for most of the story, you'll see scenes cut directly from the anime, and only when the story reached the manga chapters (the anime was in filler hell at the time) did they return to using actual in game cutscenes until the end (which are beautiful).

•CUT CONTENT
As I said, the game had to cut corners a lot and that means cutting actual gameplay content (like bosses sections) which were originally featured in the first trailers.

•THE ONLINE
It was always bad. There is no way around it. It has delay based netcode and you will have connectivity issues more often than not. However the fun lies in playing with friends in local multiplayer. That's the best experience.

NOW LET'S SEE THE GOOD THINGS:
•The bosses are SUPERB. And I mean it. The best graphics and scenes are from the actual boss fights. High resolution and with a lot of variety, it's clear where all the effort and budget went;
•It has A LOT of characters. Just choose your favourites because it has so many;
•It has a lot of offline modes: VS, tournament, story mode, adventure mode, training, survival mode. You'll have your money's worth.

AND NOW THE BEST THING:
Road to Boruto is A MUST buy for this game. You know why? Because it incorporate everything good CC2 can do when it has the time and the budget. You have your free roaming story which isn't that long and 99% of the dialogues are voiced. It has high resolution graphics and all the cutscenes have the same quality of the Boss Fights cutscenes. It's incredible if you compare them to the blurry low res cutscenes from the Main Story mode. Overall, this expansion is what the entire main story mode was supposed to look like. The quality is off the charts and you can tell even by the unique UI to this mode.

CONCLUSION:
Storm 4, even with a lot of problems, is a special game. It was the first to adapt the ending of the manga even before the anime and it nailed it. It has a lot of characters, a lot of offline modes and you will be having a lot of fun. So yeah, I TOTALLY RECOMMEND!

The Pros:
[list]
[*]Good narrative and solid storyline - As possibly the final game in the NUNS series, this is indeed quite a good "wrap-up" to the Naruto Storms franchise. Their own adaptation of the Naruto story is quite impressive, and equally emotional and touching. 

[*]60FPS FINALLY - The addition of the 60fps feature is definitely the most attractive aspect of this game, compared to its predecessors. The game just feels completely different now. Fighting is more intense and fast, and the game itself runs smoother in every way. I depised the dreadfully long loading screens in Storm 3 and Revolution. 30FPS just made everything worse.

[*]Smoother gameplay/cutscenes - even prior to the 60fps patch, the game itself loaded significantly faster than its predecessors. The previous games were a headache as I personally hated the slow loading screens between fights. Fighting games should be smooth, and the transitions between menu/character screens to the actual fight should be quick and/or seamless. 

[*]The graphics - This game is aesthetically appealing. CC2 has actually always done a fantastic job with the Naruto NUNS series, and the character models are always detailed and stays true to their anime and manga counterparts. It's crisp, it's clear, and it's accurate. The jutsus (especially ultimates) are flashy, novel, and cool. I think it's gotten to the point of a DBZ level of overkill, but I guess that's the charm of an "ultimate jutsu", right?

[*]Relatively big roster - the term "RELATIVELY" isn't loosely used here. Aside from a few duplicates, this game is still the single biggest NUNS game to date, so it's not like I have something better to compare to. I'm satifised with what we got, relatively.
[/list]


The Cons:
[list]
[*]The price - CC2 insists on maintaining the retail price tag despite all the recent mixed reviews. If you want the game to sell better, lower the retail price, and go on sale more. This game sells well on sale, but I don't really think it's selling too well if it maintains the retail price tag and that ridiculous price tag for the "whole game + Boruto expansion"

[*]Season Pass is yet another marketing scheme - Season Pass owners got screwed over, the Boruto expansion was unfortunately released as a standalone expansion.

[*]No Ultrawide support anymore? - 21:9 support removed since the newest update. I mean come on, I'm sure there's a good percentage of us who has ultrawide monitors, having support past 16;9 resolutions is a MUST for modern games.

[*]Expansion content doesn't justify the price tag - The Boruto Expansion feels half-assed, does anyone else also feel that the cutscenes are short, the boss fights are generic and bland, and the instant action sequences are very dull and easy? NUNS thrive on the gorgeous cutscenes and IA sequences, but CC2 decided to just be lazy this time around. The one last thing they have to do to a game they may just abandon altogether, and they decided to half-ass it. Such a bummer.
[/list]

I wasn't going to write a review for this game, but there seems to be a huge misconception about what this game is, and so I thought I would clear it up.

There is a TLDR at the end, as this is fairly long, and I've split it up into four sections, one on gameplay, one on the single player, one on the technical issues, and then one on the gripes I do have with the game.

GAMEPLAY-

To start with, this game is purely fan service.  This is not meant to be a truly competitive fighting game.  Anyone who has played any of these games will know this.  But if you haven't, than know that to start.  But this is a good thing.  

As I said this game is fan service.  It would make zero sense for pre time skip naruto to be as strong as Six Paths Madara.  They weren't even comparable in the manga/anime, why would they be in the game.  Lee would never be able to beat The Fourth, and Hinata would get crushed by Nagato every single time.

But that makes those moments when this happens EPIC.  You feel amazing beating Sasuke The Last as Lee, or Madara as Kiba.  It shouldn't happen, but it did and it feels great.  You know you are the under dog going in, and that makes it so much better when you win anyway.

The next thing I would say is that you shouldn't let the somewhat basic mechanics that the game has, for a lack of depth.  It is true that you will be smashing your B or Circle button the most, and your combos have more to do with properly timed cancels of limited number.  You are also severely limited in your Chakra, and that can be a game ender if you are against a good opponent.

People will run away and bait you out until you fall into the combo that they know will end the game.  They will be cheap, they will spam the OP characters.  How is this any different than how this would go in a real fight with these characters.  

I know that there are a lot of people that like these games, but don't actually read or watch the manga/anime, but those that have, should not at all be surprised in this.  The game finds it's depth, in the quite likely accidental way that it is played.

You have to have a strategy.  You have to feel out your opponent.  You have to set a trap for them and win.  How many episodes and chapters of this show have involved that very thing.  You think one side is loosing, clearly getting shashed by their opponent.  Only to then realize that it has all been a set up, and they have their enemy right where they want them.  

While a great deal of a Shinobi's power does come from their jutsu, and how strong of said jutsu they can use, a great deal of their victories, come from the decisions made, and their ability to follow their strengths, and strategies.  

A duel between shinobi is just as much a mental game as it is a physical one.  And this game does a great job of representing this to the player.  If you create a synergistic team that complements each other, and know how to use them, you can beat anyone as long as you play to their strengths, and don't try to do things that they can't do.

SINGLE PLAYER-

As a huge fan of the show, this is a big draw to me, even though it is short.  It is very well done.  There is honestly more cut scenes and dialogue than fighting going on, but it still felt good.  I think it took me about 10 hours to finish the story, doing the few side story things along the way.  It could easily be done in a handful of hours I feel if you were to skip through it all.  

The way they blend the game play into the cinematics is jarring though.  As the Anime has not finished, only the manga, there were no scenes from the show that they could use for the cinematics, and so they are rendered in game, and use the same models as the ones you use to play.  This odd blending can make it a bit hard to stay immersed fully, but that is a small complaint, and while it can be arguable as to how good of a practice it is, I can see the value in using assets from the show that are already made for you.  It cuts costs, from a business stand point, but it also minimalizes your work, you don't have to painstakingly recreate these scenes, and then get torn apart because you got some parts wrong.  There is nothing worse than a developer instilling their "vision" of a story that has already been told, and making it worse because of their changes.  And they don't do that here.  

I would caution you though, since the Anime has not finished, and doesn't look like it will be any time soon, you may want to hold off on this game until you can read the manga.  There is a lot less said in the game than in the shows and while the game does get it right still, I would consider it a spoiler, as there are definitely parts towards the end that will be really great to watch for the first time as an anime instead.  I wish I could say that you should still get it and it would be worth it, but you have to play the story to unlock the characters, so if you didn't it wouldn't be a full experience, and you would be lacking the more powerful iterations of the characters.

But if you want to have a more interactive experience with the story than watching it, I think they did a great job at providing that.  It was a fun way to experience the story, and they did a good job keeping it varied, it isn't just cut scenes followed by a battle.  You do have a little bit of a mix up with QTE sequences, as well as larger scales battles that happen that are essentially horde style missions, but on a smaller scale, and with more of a linear movement through it, instead of camping in one spot.

TECHINCAL-

The game runs alright in single player.  But as is fairly well known and documented in most of the reviews, the net code is bad, and your online experience definitely will vary.  I've had it be great on some days, and horrible on others.  Unfortunately that has become the norm for these kinds of games though, there are very few examples of fighting games that have a good online experience.  And most of the ones that do aren't ports, they were made for the PC.  It's definitely worth bringing it up, and it is the sole reason why I wouldn't recommend it at full price.  However, it is something that I think a lot of people will be used to if they frequently play fighting games online.  

COMPLAINTS- 

I do feel like the character roster is kind of bull shit.  There are something like 64 different characters, most of them have multiple versions with usually only slight differences between their moves.  And while I don't think that the power difference between some of them matter that much, it really doesn't feel like it has as big of a character pool as it does.  With the different variations of them it has something around 109 characters not including the ones you can only get from pre order.

Which is my next complaint, and something that very nearly made me not want to buy it.  Especially in a fighting game, you should never ever ever have to pre order in order to get all of the characters.  It's absolutely unacceptable.  From what I have seen, Boruto and Sarada aren't super strong or anything, but I don't know about Hokage Kakashi.  I haven't seem him much.  The problem though is that they are characters that we can not access.  We shouldn't be punished because we were smart consumers that waited to purchase the game.  

TLDR-

The game gets it's depth not from intricate and hard to execute combo's, but from the tactical decisions you have to make, as much as people hate it, running away is a legitimate strategy, setting your opponent up for the finishing move is much more important than getting off that infinite combo for the win, and you will win more if you don't just chase those combos.  Unfortunately the game runs poorly, and the online experience is lackluster.  

Buy it on sale, especially if you are a fan of the show, but the online play definitely makes it hard to recommend for full price.

Before I start, this is MY opinion of the game. Everyone has different opinions and views of this game and thats fine by me!

First off, I was not expecting to actually be able to play this game since I know my computer is not that good in specs and graphics and I just wanted to have it whenever I am able to update my computer. But I got lucky since I tried the game out anyway and was able to play it at around 20-25 fps, which I can personally deal with. 

Singleplayer: 

I really enjoyed the story mode a lot. Great fight scenes especially with the boss battles and quick times events. The only thing that I did not like was many of the cutscenes just have still images with voice overs compared to the awesome CGI ones. There is still some CGI cutscenes but compared to Naruto Ultimate Ninja Storm 3 (which was all CGI), it left me disappointed. 

Free Battle is off course what it sounds like, able to battle with any characters you want which is fun. The different combat moves and special moves are awesome to see, with many big explosions. Many different characters to choose from as well which are easy to pick up since they follow the same combat input combinations. There are also other modes such as survival which can keep you occupied. 

In adventure mode, you can use Naruto (and if you have the DLC like me, use Shikamaru with Garra coming later) which allows you to explore the different locations such as Konoha while having a main quest to do along with fun side quests mixed in adding to more content. 

Collection is there to see everything you have bought from the Bandi Store including pictures for your multiplayer card to new costumes from past games for your characters. It is a lot of content to buy and again would keep you busy to get all the content.

Multiplayer:

I do not play multiplayer since my game has slow fps. But if you do go into the multiplayer menu, there are special events that is only singleplayer which they update about every week that you can gain certain awards so that is pretty cool, especially for someone like me who is not really a big fan of multiplayer anyway. 

All in all, I really enjoy this game and being a Naruto fan this is pretty sweet. Personally, I give it a 8.5/10.

It's 2019 and this game is still one of the most enjoyable anime arena fighters out there with outstanding visuals that emulates watching the actual show. If you enjoy over-the-top battles in 3D to go with a game that's noob-friendly to all newcomers willing to give it a try, then you should try this game out whether or not you're a hardcore Naruto fan or just someone who's interested in trying out a niche anime fighting game.

Pros:
- Stunning anime-like visuals in both cutscenes and battles
- Easy to pick up fighting mechanics with tag-team leader switching style
- Fun and intense Story Mode battles with interactive QTEs
- Biggest character roster in the Storm series

Cons:
- Adventure Mode is a dull RPG experience
- First half of Story Mode are just slideshows ripped from the anime with voices and effects
- Online Mode seems dead around this time
- Difficult for a non-fan to get into the lore

TLDR; this game is a big fanservice to fans of Naruto but that shouldn't stop non-fans for trying it out as it has competent fighting game mechanics that is accessible to everyone regardless of skill to go along with compelling 3D visuals and presentation that's one of the best in the history of anime games. 7/10
